claims.statement: Monorepo development uses uv for interpreters/environments and per-package Makefiles as the source of truth for commands; uv provisions the correct Python interpreter automatically so there is no global Python version to pin.

Repository tests should be network-free and deterministic under `tests/unit_tests/`, with `tests/integration_tests/` reserved for networked integration contracts; unaccepted pytest warnings fail the suite.
The ACP and Talon standard `make test` targets disable network sockets; Talon's target first runs WhatsApp bridge Node tests.
Each package has its own `pyproject.toml`, `Makefile`, and README, and its local source and tests are the authoritative place to determine how to change and validate that package.

Package requirements, uv sibling-source mappings, and package-local lockfiles are distinct layers: published dependency constraints are separate from development checkout wiring and generated project resolution.

Talon publishes direct requirements on `deepagents>=0.7.41` and `deepagents-code>=0.2.13,<1.0.0`, while history embedding adapters and MongoDB/PostgreSQL support are optional extras rather than base-host dependencies.

The targeted lockfile refresher computes the changed package and transitive reverse consumers from local uv path sources, locks each with the repository checker's selected interpreter, and selects Python 3.14 for Talon, dcode, ACP, and evals.

The targeted lockfile checker checks only packages named by supplied paths (or all discovered packages when none are supplied), and reports an executable non-check `uv lock` repair command for an out-of-date lock.
The `libs` fan-out Makefile maps dcode, evals, and Talon to Python 3.14 and all other packages to Python 3.12, so its `lock-check` target is not a CI-equivalent lock validation route for ACP.
The `deepagents` SDK supports Python `>=3.11,<4.0`, while dcode (`deepagents-code`) requires Python `>=3.14,<3.15` and pins its SDK dependency to `deepagents==0.7.41`.
The reusable Check Lockfiles workflow runs the targeted checker with no path arguments, so it validates every discovered package lockfile in CI.
The release manifest maintains separate release baselines for `libs/deepagents`, `libs/acp`, `libs/code`, `libs/talon`, and each listed partner package.
dcode's unit-test target disables network sockets, while its `integration_test` target runs the integration-test directory without that socket restriction.
QuickJS supports Python `>=3.11,<4.0`, publishes `deepagents>=0.7.41,<0.8.0`, and uses an editable local SDK source mapping during checkout development.
Talon's `media` and `media-cpu` extras conflict, and its source mappings use the CPU PyTorch index for the latter on Linux.
The release manifest baselines are deepagents 0.7.41, ACP 0.1.0, dcode 0.2.14, Talon 0.1.1, and partner packages Daytona 0.0.9, Modal 0.0.8, Runloop 0.0.7, Vercel 0.0.2, and QuickJS 0.4.0.
The `libs/` packages separate core SDK, ACP integration, evals/Harbor, dcode, Talon, and provider or sandbox partner responsibilities.
Release-please creates or updates a separate draft release PR per managed package from conventional commits on `main`; merging that release PR triggers the publish and GitHub-release workflow.
If dcode requires new SDK functionality, its exact `deepagents==` pin must be updated in the feature PR rather than deferred to release time.

The ACP distribution is version 0.1.0, supports Python `>=3.11,<4.0`, and publishes dependencies on `deepagents` and Agent Client Protocol `>=1.0.0,<2.0.0`; its editable SDK mapping is checkout-only wiring.

The evals distribution is version 0.0.1 and requires Python `>=3.14,<3.15`; its published requirements include deepagents and deepagents-code, while its development source mappings connect local dcode, SDK, and QuickJS checkouts.
